prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1001; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured's policy is active and the claimant's vehicle was involved in a left-turn collision at an intersection. The insured driver is named on the policy, and the reported loss falls within the coverage period.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the impact. Photos taken at the scene show damage consistent with the described sequence, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection shows most of the damage lines up with the impact described by both parties. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: The claimant, who is not represented, reported neck and back strain. The injury pattern matches the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and no prior injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 5: In each conversation the claimant has given the same account of the collision and the sequence of events. Statements remain consistent across all contacts to date.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course for soft-tissue injuries of this kind. Care has tapered as the claimant's symptoms improved, and the treating provider's notes reflect steady recovery.

Entry 7: Liability review is ongoing based on the photos, police report, and vehicle damage. The file is progressing normally, and no further coverage questions have been identified at this stage.
